title: Degree-zero compact support for constructible adic sheaves
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$ and an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $G\in\Sh_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ be a constructible sheaf in degree zero [def-weil-constructible-heart], in the derived-complete, rationalized, common-finite-stage category of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Write $\mathbf 1_X$ for its coefficient unit. Ordinary global adic sections mean $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)}(\mathbf 1_X,G)$.

The compact-to-ordinary comparison induces a natural injective linear map
$$\alpha_{X,G}:H_c^0(X,G)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\Sh_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)}(\mathbf 1_X,G).$$
For every $c\in H_c^0(X,G)$ there is a closed subset $Z\subseteq X$, proper over $k$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base], such that the restriction of $\alpha_{X,G}(c)$ to $X\setminus Z$ is zero. The section comparison agrees with ordinary restriction of sections on every open subscheme. For a lisse restriction, its section is the ordinary lisse adic section under the realization and $H^0$ comparison of [lem-a1-degree-zero-compact-support-sections].

source.place: Proposition 18.3(b), pp. 120–121, after Definition 18.1; adic extension and realization are part of this statement, formulated using Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15, not asserted to be the literal finite-torsion proposition
